about: Controlled skill catalog for the clarify:interview trigger-discrimination harness. The three clarify skills carry their REAL frontmatter descriptions (verbatim); the distractors are realistic competing skills whose descriptions plausibly attract the negative queries. This isolates description discriminative power from a live machine's skill-budget contention (see trigger-eval-README.md). Keep the clarify descriptions in sync with the SKILL.md frontmatter.

skills.name: clarify:interview
skills.description: This skill should be used when the user's request or requirement is ambiguous and needs an iterative interview to become actionable — vague feature requests ("add notifications"), incomplete bug reports ("the export is broken"), underspecified tasks and migrations ("make it faster", "convert this to TypeScript"), or any build request the user hasn't fully thought through. Trigger on "clarify requirements", "refine requirements", "요구사항 명확히", "요구사항 정리", "요구사항 인터뷰", "인터뷰해줘", "interview me", "ask me questions before building", "make this clearer", "spec this out", "scope this", "/clarify:interview". Turns vague inputs into concrete specs and surfaces considerations the user hasn't thought of. For strategy blind spots use unknown; for content-vs-form reframing use metamedium.

skills.name: clarify:unknown
skills.description: This skill should be used when the user provides a strategy, plan, or decision document and wants to surface hidden assumptions and blind spots using the Known/Unknown 4-quadrant framework. Trigger on "known unknown", "4분면 분석", "blind spots", "what am I missing", "뭘 놓치고 있지", "전략 점검", "가정 점검", "quadrant analysis". For requirement clarification use interview; for content-vs-form reframing use metamedium.

skills.name: clarify:metamedium
skills.description: This skill should be used when the key question is whether to optimize content (what) or redesign form (how/medium). Trigger on "내용 vs 형식", "content vs form", "metamedium", "형식을 바꿔볼까", "새로운 포맷", "perspective shift", "diminishing returns". For requirement clarification use interview; for strategy blind spots use unknown.

skills.name: code-review
skills.description: Review the current diff or a pull request for correctness bugs, regressions, and reuse/simplification cleanups. Use when the user asks to review code, check a PR, or find bugs before merging.

skills.name: investigate
skills.description: Systematic debugging with root-cause investigation. Use when something is broken, a test fails, an error or stack trace appears, or the user asks why code misbehaves and wants the underlying cause found and fixed.

skills.name: run-tests
skills.description: Run the project's test suite and report failures. Use when the user asks to run tests, check if tests pass, or diagnose a failing test command like npm test or pytest.

skills.name: blog-figure
skills.description: Generate a static PNG figure for a blog post — flow diagrams, comparisons, charts, infographics, concept diagrams. Use when the user wants any visual for a blog or MDX file: 그림, 도표, 다이어그램, 차트, 인포그래픽, 시각화.

skills.name: deep-research
skills.description: Fan-out web research with adversarial verification and a cited report. Use when the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked answer to a research question about the outside world.

skills.name: design-mockup
skills.description: Create or edit UI designs, screens, components, and mockups in Figma, or turn a design into code. Use when the user wants to mock up a screen, show color/layout options, or generate a visual interface.

skills.name: doc-writer
skills.description: Write or update documentation — README sections, guides, API docs, changelogs — from existing code or the user's outline. Use when the user asks to add or improve docs, write a README section, or document a feature.

skills.name: simplify
skills.description: Refactor recently changed code for clarity, reuse, and efficiency without changing behavior. Use for a tidy/refactor pass on code the user just wrote.

skills.name: ship
skills.description: Ship workflow: run tests, review the diff, bump the version, update the changelog, commit, push, and open a PR. Use when the user says code is ready, wants to deploy, push, or create a PR.

skills.name: translate
skills.description: Translate text between languages while preserving meaning and tone. Use when the user asks to translate a document, message, or UI string.

skills.name: humanize-korean
skills.description: Rewrite AI-generated Korean text to read as human-written, removing translationese and mechanical patterns. Use when the user wants to remove the 'AI 티' from Korean writing.
